name: Refreshed in a dry season
promise: Six days for dry seasons, on the quickening Spirit, the well, the river and the roots that keep you watered.
why: Dryness is not the end of a walk with God; in Scripture it is often the place where wells are sung open and rivers are found. Across these six sessions the Apostle teaches why prayer feels dry when the Spirit has not quickened us, how worship makes the dry well spring up, how the river of God satisfies the deepest thirst and comes in measures, and how roots and rest keep a believer watered. If you feel empty, stale or far from God, come and drink again.

days.theme: When prayer feels dry: the quickening Spirit
days.key_quote: If God touches you and you cannot sense his touch, it means you are unconscious to God.

days.theme: Worship makes the dry well spring up
days.key_quote: A well that was dry initially, but was provoked by a song.

days.theme: The river that satisfies the deepest thirst
days.key_quote: One of the characteristics of the God life is that it satisfies.

days.theme: Measures of the river: ankle-deep is not enough
days.key_quote: There are measures of interaction with this river.

days.theme: Take root downward: depth before height
days.key_quote: It is only those that have the experience of depth that are entitled to the manifestation of height.

days.theme: Rest for the weary, refreshing for the dry
days.key_quote: The river conditions the environment of heaven, and it makes it glad.
